title: Safety, Alignment & the Research Frontier
blurb: What's at the moving edge of AI engineering in 2026. Alignment, attacks, interpretability, reasoning models, long context, the open research problems — and the career & community node that closes the roadmap.

nodes.label: Alignment basics
nodes.description: What 'alignment' means in practice, the helpful/harmless/honest framing, refusal training, the gap between training-time and deployment-time alignment.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why an aligned model can still be misused and where alignment training breaks.

resources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
resources.author: Bai et al. (Anthropic)
resources.annotation: The CAI paper. The clearest open description of how a frontier lab trains for helpfulness-plus-harmlessness, and a working alternative to vanilla RLHF.

resources.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
resources.author: Ouyang et al. (OpenAI)
resources.annotation: The InstructGPT paper, reread with the alignment-not-just-tuning lens. The starting point for the modern post-training stack.

nodes.label: Jailbreaks & prompt injection
nodes.description: Direct jailbreaks, indirect (data-driven) prompt injection, exfiltration via tool outputs, the OWASP-for-LLM threat model. The attack surface every AI engineer should know.
nodes.doneWhen: You can list five jailbreak / injection vectors and the production mitigations for each.

resources.title: Prompt Injection — Simon Willison's running coverage
resources.author: Simon Willison
resources.annotation: The longest-running practitioner coverage. Direct, indirect, exfiltration via tool outputs — keeps tracking the field.

resources.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
resources.author: Zou et al.
resources.annotation: GCG — the optimized-suffix jailbreak that demonstrated transferable attacks. The paper to read for the rigorous-attack lens.

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
resources.annotation: The taxonomy of LLM-app vulnerabilities. Pair with Willison's writing; the OWASP doc is what your security team will reference.

nodes.label: Red-teaming
nodes.description: Structured red-teaming of LLM products, automated red-teaming, the pre-launch eval playbook. What 'security review' means for a model.
nodes.doneWhen: You can plan a structured red-team exercise for an LLM product launch.

resources.title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
resources.author: Perez et al. (DeepMind)
resources.annotation: The paper that established automated red-teaming. The patterns recur in every modern eval pipeline.

resources.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
resources.annotation: The vendor-neutral framework. Useful when red-teaming has to interface with compliance or risk-management functions.

nodes.label: Mechanistic interpretability
nodes.description: Probing inside the model: features, circuits, sparse autoencoders, induction heads. Where the field is trying to make 'understanding a model' a real thing.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe what an SAE feature is and why mech-interp matters for safety.

resources.title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
resources.author: Elhage et al. (Anthropic)
resources.annotation: The foundational paper of modern mech-interp. The residual-stream framing carries through everything that came after.

resources.title: Towards Monosemanticity
resources.author: Bricken et al. (Anthropic)
resources.annotation: Sparse autoencoders for finding monosemantic features. The paper that put mech-interp on the practical-tools map.

resources.title: Neel Nanda — Mech-interp tutorials
resources.annotation: The practitioner's on-ramp. If the papers are too dense, start here.

nodes.label: Reasoning models (o-style)
nodes.description: Test-time compute, chain-of-thought as a training target, the OpenAI o-series and the open replications. The newest capability paradigm and how to deploy it.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why a reasoning model trades latency for accuracy and when that trade is worth it.

resources.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
resources.author: DeepSeek-AI
resources.annotation: The open reasoning-model paper. The recipe (pure-RL on verifiable rewards, then SFT) is the clearest open replication of the o-series approach.

resources.title: Learning to Reason with LLMs (OpenAI o1)
resources.author: OpenAI
resources.annotation: The o1 announcement post. The clearest framing of test-time compute as a scaling axis.

nodes.label: Long context techniques
nodes.description: Sliding window attention, position interpolation, YaRN, ring attention, the 1M-context frontier. Why long context isn't just 'more memory'.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe one technique that extends context length and what it costs.

resources.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models
resources.author: Peng et al.
resources.annotation: YaRN — the RoPE-extension recipe that became the open default for context extension.

resources.title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers
resources.author: Liu et al.
resources.annotation: Ring attention — the parallelism trick that enables million-token contexts. The right reference when you wonder how 1M context windows actually run.

nodes.label: Open research areas
nodes.description: World models, embodied agents, continual learning, robust generalization, alignment science. The active frontiers that may reshape engineering practice next.
nodes.doneWhen: You can name three open research problems and explain why they matter to engineering.

resources.title: Anthropic — Core Views on AI Safety
resources.annotation: The strategic frame from one frontier lab. The 'when, why, and what' framing for safety research.

resources.title: Lilian Weng's blog
resources.author: Lilian Weng
resources.annotation: The single best running survey of frontier ML research, with deeply-thought essays on attention, agents, RLHF, and more.

resources.title: Sebastian Raschka's Magazine
resources.author: Sebastian Raschka
resources.annotation: The monthly newsletter that summarizes what's actually new in the field. The right way to track the frontier without drowning.

nodes.label: Career, community & staying current
nodes.description: How to keep up (papers, newsletters, conferences), how to contribute, how to interview. Peers: llm-interview-prep for interview preparation; build-your-own-ai for hands-on practice.
nodes.doneWhen: You have a sustainable monthly routine for staying current — and you've contributed once.

resources.title: llm-interview-prep
resources.annotation: The peer roadmap for AI-engineer interview preparation. Open when you're about to interview.

resources.title: build-your-own-ai
resources.annotation: Hands-on 'build it yourself' projects (transformer, RAG, agent harness, etc.). The companion to this roadmap for learners-by-doing.

resources.title: AlphaSignal — daily AI newsletter
resources.annotation: The shortest sustainable daily-ish read for AI engineering. Pair with weekly Sebastian Raschka / Latent Space.

resources.title: Latent Space podcast
resources.annotation: The AI-engineer podcast. Interviews with the people shipping the systems you'll be reading about a month later.
